```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

## Purpose

Reads the split conversations and sorts every participant into groups on four yes/no variables. Each variable is built by reading the turn text itself every time the file is knit, so the groups always match the current text.

**Input:** `05_Q4_3_conversations_wide_deid.csv`, one row per participant, with each turn in its own column (`human_1`, `ai_1`, `human_2`, ...).

**Outputs**

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `data/processed/06_Q4_3_binary_categories.xlsx` | Sheet `binary_vars`: `pid` plus the four variables. Sheet `audit`: the matched disease terms, medication names, counts and lengths behind each code. Sheet `codebook`: definitions and coding rules |
| `output/06_Q4_3_binary-categories/binary_pies.png` | Pie chart for each variable |

**Variables**

| Variable | 1 | 0 | Missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| `human_mentions_disease` | Participant names a disease or condition in any of their turns | No condition named | No participant text |
| `human_multi_turn` | Participant wrote more than one turn | Participant wrote one turn | No participant turns |
| `ai_multi_med` | AI names more than one distinct medication | AI names exactly one medication | AI names no medication (not applicable) |
| `human_1_long` | First participant message longer than the median | At or below the median | No first message |

## Read the data

```{r read}
wide <- readr::read_csv(in_file, col_types = cols(.default = col_character()), na = c("", "NA"))

# Turn text columns only (not the _n_words / _notes columns), in turn order
turn_cols <- function(prefix) {
  cols <- grep(paste0("^", prefix, "_[0-9]+$"), names(wide), value = TRUE)
  cols[order(as.integer(sub(".*_", "", cols)))]
}
human_cols <- turn_cols("human")
ai_cols    <- turn_cols("ai")

cat(nrow(wide), "participants\n")
cat("human turn columns:", paste(range(human_cols), collapse = " to "), "\n")
cat("ai turn columns:   ", paste(range(ai_cols), collapse = " to "), "\n")
```

## Word lists and settings

Write every term in lowercase. Matching ignores case, matches whole words only, and treats apostrophes as optional, so `crohn's` also matches `crohns`.

**Diseases and conditions.** The list covers named diseases and diagnoses, not symptoms. Words like *headache*, *rash*, *fever* or *pain* are left out on purpose, so "I have a headache" is coded 0. Add a symptom to the list if your definition should include it.

- `DISEASE_TERMS`: matched in any case.
- `DISEASE_ACRONYMS`: matched only in capitals, because some are also everyday words (`MS`, `ADD`, `AIDS`).
- `DISEASE_SUFFIXES`: also catches medical words by their ending (*-itis*, *-osis*, ...), so misspellings and conditions missing from the list are still picked up. `SUFFIX_EXCLUDE` blocks everyday words with the same endings.
- `DISEASE_HEAD_WORDS`: catches phrases such as "sinus infection" or "vitamin d deficiency". Leading filler words ("a", "my", "this") are dropped, so "an infection" alone does not count.

**Medications.** `MED_TERMS` maps each name to one standard name, so a brand and its generic count once (*Advil* and *ibuprofen* are both `ibuprofen`). Add entries as `"name" = "standard name"`.

- `MED_SUFFIXES` catches generic drug names by their ending (*-pril*, *-statin*, *-cillin*, ...) when they are not on the list.
- `INCLUDE_SUPPLEMENTS`: vitamins and supplements such as melatonin count as medications only when `TRUE`.
- `INCLUDE_DRUG_CLASSES`: general class words (*antibiotics*, *NSAIDs*) count as medications only when `TRUE`. They are off by default because "an NSAID like ibuprofen" would otherwise count twice.

## Matching functions

You shouldn't need to edit this section. Everything it uses comes from the lists above.

```{r functions}
strip_apos <- function(x) gsub("['\u2019]", "", x)
escape_regex <- function(x) gsub("([.|()^{}+$*?\\[\\]\\\\])", "\\\\\\1", x, perl = TRUE)
norm_term <- function(x) trimws(gsub("[[:space:]-]+", " ", tolower(strip_apos(x))))
has_text <- function(x) !is.na(x) & trimws(x) != ""

# Whole-word pattern for a list of terms; spaces and hyphens are interchangeable;
# longest first so "type 2 diabetes" wins over "diabetes"
build_term_pattern <- function(terms) {
  terms <- unique(strip_apos(terms))
  terms <- terms[order(-nchar(terms))]
  alts <- vapply(terms, function(t) {
    parts <- strsplit(trimws(t), "[[:space:]-]+")[[1]]
    paste(escape_regex(parts), collapse = "[\\s\\-]+")
  }, character(1))
  paste0("(?<!\\w)(?:", paste(alts, collapse = "|"), ")(?!\\w)")
}

# Medication lookup (raw name -> standard name), built from the settings above
med_lookup <- MED_TERMS
if (INCLUDE_SUPPLEMENTS)  med_lookup <- c(med_lookup, SUPPLEMENT_TERMS)
if (INCLUDE_DRUG_CLASSES) med_lookup <- c(med_lookup, DRUG_CLASS_TERMS)
names(med_lookup) <- norm_term(names(med_lookup))
med_known <- unique(c(names(med_lookup), unname(med_lookup)))

DISEASE_PAT <- regex(build_term_pattern(DISEASE_TERMS), ignore_case = TRUE)
ACRONYM_PAT <- regex(build_term_pattern(DISEASE_ACRONYMS))                       # capitals only
SUFFIX_PAT  <- regex(paste0("\\b[a-z]{3,}(?:", paste(DISEASE_SUFFIXES, collapse = "|"), ")\\b"), ignore_case = TRUE)
HEAD_PAT    <- regex(paste0("\\b((?:[a-z0-9]+\\s+){1,2})(", paste(DISEASE_HEAD_WORDS, collapse = "|"), ")\\b"),
                     ignore_case = TRUE)
MED_PAT     <- regex(build_term_pattern(names(med_lookup)), ignore_case = TRUE)
MED_SUF_PAT <- regex(paste0("\\b[a-z]+(?:", paste(MED_SUFFIXES, collapse = "|"), ")\\b"), ignore_case = TRUE)


find_diseases <- function(text) {
  if (!has_text(text)) return(character(0))
  t <- strip_apos(text)
  hits <- norm_term(str_extract_all(t, DISEASE_PAT)[[1]])
  hits <- c(hits, str_extract_all(t, ACRONYM_PAT)[[1]])
  suf  <- tolower(str_extract_all(t, SUFFIX_PAT)[[1]])
  hits <- c(hits, setdiff(suf, SUFFIX_EXCLUDE))
  heads <- str_match_all(t, HEAD_PAT)[[1]]
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(heads))) {             # "sinus infection", "vitamin d deficiency"
    words <- strsplit(tolower(trimws(heads[i, 2])), "\\s+")[[1]]
    while (length(words) > 0 && words[1] %in% STOPWORDS) words <- words[-1]
    if (length(words) > 0) hits <- c(hits, paste(c(words, tolower(heads[i, 3])), collapse = " "))
  }
  sort(unique(hits))
}

find_meds <- function(text) {
  if (!has_text(text)) return(character(0))
  t <- strip_apos(text)
  found <- unname(med_lookup[norm_term(str_extract_all(t, MED_PAT)[[1]])])
  suf <- tolower(str_extract_all(t, MED_SUF_PAT)[[1]])
  suf <- suf[nchar(suf) >= MED_SUFFIX_MIN_LEN & !suf %in% MED_SUFFIX_EXCLUDE & !suf %in% med_known]
  sort(unique(c(found, suf)))
}
```

### Check the matching on made-up text

Edit these sentences to see what the lists catch before trusting the real results.

```{r check-matching}
checks <- c(
  "do i have type 2 diabetes or is it just prediabetes",
  "my mom has Crohns and MS, could that be related",
  "i think its tendonitis from running",
  "I have a headache and a rash",                                   # symptoms only -> nothing
  "is it ok to take Advil with my lisinopril",
  "Ibuprofen (Advil) or acetaminophen can help, or ask about a rosuvastatin alternative.",
  "a vitamin d deficiency can cause fatigue"
)
tibble(text = checks,
       diseases = vapply(checks, \(x) paste(find_diseases(x), collapse = "; "), character(1)),
       meds     = vapply(checks, \(x) paste(find_meds(x), collapse = "; "), character(1))) |>
  kable()
```

## Build the binary variables

```{r build}
hm <- as.matrix(wide[human_cols])
am <- as.matrix(wide[ai_cols])
collect <- function(row, fn) sort(unique(unlist(lapply(row, fn))))

# 1. Participant names a disease or condition (any participant turn)
human_any_text <- apply(hm, 1, \(r) any(has_text(r)))
disease_terms  <- apply(hm, 1, \(r) paste(collect(r, find_diseases), collapse = "; "))

# 2. More than one participant turn (counted from the text columns)
n_human <- apply(hm, 1, \(r) sum(has_text(r)))
n_human[n_human == 0] <- NA

# 3. AI names more than one distinct medication (all AI turns, including ai_0)
ai_meds   <- apply(am, 1, \(r) collect(r, find_meds), simplify = FALSE)
ai_n_meds <- lengths(ai_meds)

# 4. Long vs short first participant message (median split)
text_length <- function(t) {
  ifelse(!has_text(t), NA_real_,
         if (LENGTH_MEASURE == "words") lengths(strsplit(trimws(t), "\\s+")) else nchar(trimws(t)))
}
first_len  <- text_length(wide$human_1)
median_len <- median(first_len, na.rm = TRUE)

binary_vars <- tibble(
  pid                    = wide$pid,
  human_mentions_disease = ifelse(!human_any_text, NA, as.integer(disease_terms != "")),
  human_multi_turn       = ifelse(is.na(n_human), NA, as.integer(n_human > 1)),
  ai_multi_med           = ifelse(ai_n_meds == 0, NA, as.integer(ai_n_meds > 1)),
  human_1_long           = ifelse(is.na(first_len), NA, as.integer(first_len > median_len))
)

audit <- tibble(
  pid                 = wide$pid,
  human_disease_terms = disease_terms,
  n_human_turns       = n_human,
  ai_med_names        = vapply(ai_meds, paste, character(1), collapse = "; "),
  ai_n_meds           = ai_n_meds,
  ai_any_med          = as.integer(ai_n_meds > 0),
  human_1_length      = first_len
)

# Cross-check the turn count against the one made in the earlier scripts
if ("n_human_turns" %in% names(wide)) {
  earlier <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(wide$n_human_turns))
  cat("Participants where the text count differs from n_human_turns:",
      sum(coalesce(n_human, 0) != coalesce(earlier, 0)), "\n")
}
cat("Median first-message length:", median_len, LENGTH_MEASURE, "\n")
```

## Check the matches

Which terms drove the disease and medication codes? Look here for false matches, then edit the lists and knit again.

```{r check-terms}
audit |>
  separate_rows(human_disease_terms, sep = "; ") |>
  filter(human_disease_terms != "") |>
  count(human_disease_terms, sort = TRUE, name = "n_participants") |>
  kable(caption = "Disease terms matched in participant turns")

audit |>
  separate_rows(ai_med_names, sep = "; ") |>
  filter(ai_med_names != "") |>
  count(ai_med_names, sort = TRUE, name = "n_participants") |>
  kable(caption = "Medication names matched in AI turns")
```

## Save the Excel file

```{r save}
codebook <- tribble(
  ~variable, ~definition, ~coding, ~notes,
  "pid", "Participant ID (de-identified)", "", "",
  "human_mentions_disease", "Participant names a disease or condition in any of their turns",
    "1 = yes, 0 = no", "Missing if no participant text. Symptoms alone do not count.",
  "human_multi_turn", "Participant wrote more than one turn",
    "1 = more than one turn, 0 = one turn", "Counted from the filled human_ text columns. Missing if no participant turns.",
  "ai_multi_med", "AI names more than one distinct medication across its turns",
    "1 = two or more, 0 = exactly one",
    paste0("Missing when the AI names no medication. Brand and generic count once. Supplements included: ",
           INCLUDE_SUPPLEMENTS, ". Drug classes included: ", INCLUDE_DRUG_CLASSES, "."),
  "human_1_long", "First participant message is longer than the median",
    "1 = above median, 0 = at or below median",
    paste0("Measured in ", LENGTH_MEASURE, " from the human_1 text. Median = ", median_len,
           ". Ties at the median are coded 0.")
)

wb <- createWorkbook()
for (sheet in c("binary_vars", "audit", "codebook")) {
  addWorksheet(wb, sheet)
  writeData(wb, sheet, get(sheet), headerStyle = createStyle(textDecoration = "bold"))
  freezePane(wb, sheet, firstRow = TRUE)
  setColWidths(wb, sheet, cols = seq_along(get(sheet)), widths = "auto")
}
addStyle(wb, "codebook", createStyle(wrapText = TRUE, valign = "top"),
         rows = 2:(nrow(codebook) + 1), cols = 1:4, gridExpand = TRUE)
setColWidths(wb, "codebook", cols = 1:4, widths = c(24, 45, 30, 60))
saveWorkbook(wb, out_file, overwrite = TRUE)
cat("Saved", out_file, "\n")
```

## Counts and pie charts

One pie per variable, showing how many participants fall in each group. Participants coded missing are left out of the pie and counted under its title. Following the Healogix chart standards, the slices use two blues: dark blue for the group coded 1 and light blue for the group coded 0. Every slice is also labeled with its group name, count and percentage, so the chart doesn't rely on color alone.

```{r counts}
var_names <- setdiff(names(binary_vars), "pid")

counts <- tibble(
  variable  = var_names,
  n_1       = vapply(var_names, \(v) sum(binary_vars[[v]] == 1, na.rm = TRUE), integer(1)),
  n_0       = vapply(var_names, \(v) sum(binary_vars[[v]] == 0, na.rm = TRUE), integer(1)),
  n_missing = vapply(var_names, \(v) sum(is.na(binary_vars[[v]])), integer(1))
) |>
  mutate(n_coded = n_1 + n_0,
         pct_1   = round(100 * n_1 / na_if(n_coded, 0), 1))

kable(counts, caption = "Participants in each group")
```

```{r pies, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 9.5}
# Plain-language titles and group names: title, label for 1, label for 0
pie_labels <- tribble(
  ~variable,                ~title,                                                    ~lab_1,          ~lab_0,
  "human_mentions_disease", "Participant named a disease",                             "Yes",           "No",
  "human_multi_turn",       "Number of participant turns",                             "More than one", "One",
  "ai_multi_med",           "Medications the AI named\n(among conversations naming any)", "Two or more", "One",
  "human_1_long",           paste0("Length of first message\n(median = ", median_len, " ", LENGTH_MEASURE, ")"),
                                                                                       "Above median",  "At or below\nmedian"
)

COLOR_1 <- "#1F4E79"   # dark blue
COLOR_0 <- "#9DC3E6"   # light blue
INK     <- "#1A1A1A"

pie_data <- counts |>
  inner_join(pie_labels, by = "variable") |>
  filter(n_coded > 0) |>
  mutate(panel = paste0(title, "\nN = ", n_coded,
                        ifelse(n_missing > 0, paste0("  |  ", n_missing, " missing, not shown"), "")),
         panel = factor(panel, levels = panel)) |>
  select(panel, n_1, n_0, lab_1, lab_0, n_coded) |>
  pivot_longer(c(n_1, n_0), names_to = "group", values_to = "n") |>
  filter(n > 0) |>
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = c("n_1", "n_0")),
         label = paste0(ifelse(group == "n_1", lab_1, lab_0), "\nn = ", n, " (", round(100 * n / n_coded), "%)"),
         prop  = n / n_coded,                 # each pie fills its own circle
         fill  = ifelse(group == "n_1", COLOR_1, COLOR_0),
         ink   = ifelse(group == "n_1", "white", INK))

if (nrow(pie_data) == 0) {
  cat("No coded participants yet, so there is nothing to chart.\n")
} else {
pies <- ggplot(pie_data, aes(x = 1, y = prop, fill = fill, group = group)) +
  geom_col(width = 1, color = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label = label, color = ink), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), size = 3.6,
            lineheight = 0.95) +
  coord_polar(theta = "y", direction = -1) +
  facet_wrap(~ panel, ncol = 2) +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  scale_color_identity() +
  labs(title = "Q4 Pulse 3: conversation groups") +
  theme_void(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 15, color = INK, margin = margin(b = 10)),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 11, color = INK, lineheight = 1.1, margin = margin(b = 6)),
        panel.spacing = unit(1.5, "lines"),
        plot.margin = margin(15, 10, 10, 10),
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA))

print(pies)
ggsave(file.path(out_dir, "binary_pies.png"), pies, width = 10, height = 9.5, dpi = 200, bg = "white")
}
```
